- **Policy**: **Account Deletion Requirement**
- **Severity**: 🔵 Suggestion
- **Files**: [AgentStorage.kt:L67](file://Z:/Codezzz/android/AndroidOpenRouterAgent/app/src/main/java/com/example/openrouteragent/AgentStorage.kt#L67), [GitHubClient.kt:L54](file://Z:/Codezzz/android/AndroidOpenRouterAgent/app/src/main/java/com/example/openrouteragent/GitHubClient.kt#L54), [MainActivity.kt:L1550](file://Z:/Codezzz/android/AndroidOpenRouterAgent/app/src/main/java/com/example/openrouteragent/MainActivity.kt#L1550), [OpenRouterSignIn.kt:L114](file://Z:/Codezzz/android/AndroidOpenRouterAgent/app/src/main/java/com/example/openrouteragent/OpenRouterSignIn.kt#L114), [OpenRouterSignIn.kt:L49](file://Z:/Codezzz/android/AndroidOpenRouterAgent/app/src/main/java/com/example/openrouteragent/OpenRouterSignIn.kt#L49)
- **Evidence**: Settings links to OpenRouter key management and starts browser authorization at OpenRouter. The exchange obtains a user-controlled OpenRouter API key and the app stores that key locally with Android Keystore. The optional GitHub connection also uses an externally issued credential. The audited app paths exposed no developer-managed app-account creation flow. Play also considers creation of an app-specific identity through an external signup flow to be account creation.

**Critic Verification**: Automatically verified (bypassed critic review). (Confidence: High)
- **Recommendation**: Complete the Data safety deletion questions using the actual production sign-up flow. If the release provisions an app-specific account through OpenRouter or any other service, provide a discoverable in-app path and a public web resource for requesting deletion of the app account and associated data. Document which data users can delete locally and how they can manage retained OpenRouter files and account data. See https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/13327111 and https://openrouter.ai/privacy.
- **References**:
  - https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10144311#account_deletion
